calls.head: Where the Ducks have the edge: the penalty kill
calls.body: The Ducks are near the top of the league for the penalty kill, and the Canucks are the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though.

surprises.head: Anaheim kept finding open men against Leevi Meriläinen
surprises.body: Meriläinen allowed 5 goals on 23 shots, worth 2.4 expected goals: 2.6 more than expected, though three of them came off a pass that set up the shooter. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 20 starts.

story.head: The Canucks finally end the skid
paras: What a comeback. The Canucks won for the first time in eleven games, after going 0-9-1. A.J. Greer opened the scoring for the Ducks late in the first. The second period was a wild one. Liam Öhgren tied it up for Vancouver early in the period, and Jeff Malott restored the Ducks’ lead 30 seconds later. Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson scored less than three minutes apart late in the period to make it 4-1. There were five goals in the third period alone. Brock Boeser cut Anaheim’s lead to 4-2 midway through the period, and Greer struck again 43 seconds later to make it 5-2 for the Ducks. Jamie Oleksiak scored once and Jonathan Lekkerimäki twice in just over five minutes with just over seven minutes left to tie it 5-5. Filip Hronek won it on the power play in overtime. Three players had three-point nights: Boeser with a goal and two assists, the Ducks’ Jackson LaCombe with three assists, and Lekkerimäki with two goals and an assist.

The Canucks owned the chances, outshooting the Ducks 33-23, and still had to sweat it out in overtime. Leevi Meriläinen made 18 saves for the Canucks, and Lukáš Dostál allowed six goals on 33 shots. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Linus Karlsson, even with Hronek’s overtime winner in the game, by our Swing measure.
Malott and Paul Cotter picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Canucks improved to 3-10-1, still last in the NHL, while the Ducks dropped to 5-6-1 but climbed to fifth in the Pacific.
